item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Joke SCP - mind-influencing game code
item.content:encoded:
Noting a PM request to take another look

You've, definitely sort of tightened this up so it feels more cohesive as a whole; but it also feels very…flat? I don't really have an idea of like, what you're intending to do with the actual narrative or how the like, situation changes over the course of the story, or what the stakes are or anything. It feels a lot more focussed on -1 as a character but without really like, giving me anything that indicates they're interesting as a character, or like, really…doing anything with the narrative?

You mention that the addendum is about 'the downfall of a Foundation monitoring team': what like, actually happens here? Is this meant as the meat of the article or is this just the appetiser before the main meal of the story?

I missed this the first time round (sorry), but how is this a joke SCP? It feels a lot more like it's 'a serious scp born out of a joke' than 'a scp which is a joke'.

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Joke SCP - mind-influencing game code
item.content:encoded:
I'm not really a fan of an idea that boils actual addictions down to 'oh it's an anomaly', particularly ones that can be as quietly harmful to people as video game addictions can be.

Beyond this, the narrative feels…unfocussed? It kinda flits around various ideas: the behavioural patterns of the SCP, the way it affects players, the list of games it was part of; and it feels like these ideas never really come together to form a single, cohesive whole. It also feels like this could really do with a like…single affected player as the focus character, like, someone we can see slipping into worse and worse patterns of behaviour and whose plight is empathetic in a way that fills us with dread as we see them descend towards some final outcome that's terrible; but my concern is that the effect of the SCP is too compulsive for this to work well. That is to say: the SCP is effectively forcing them to become addicted, so there's no real like, choice or ability for them to like resist this or anything; whereas if the SCP was more…'seductive', then you can really like, have them be conflicted about whether they should stop and really give the narrative the conflict it needs that way.

I don't think it necessarily needs to be focussed in this specific manner; but it does feel like it all needs to come together in a way that makes it feel like this is telling a single, coherent story and it doesn't quite yet do that, for me.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Joke SCP - mind-influencing game code
item.content:encoded:
A seemingly insignificant script which mysteriously appears in popular online multiplayers, generates a user account of which in game exposure can influence the mind.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Joke SCP

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch:

  • SCP-XXXX is a script
  • SCP-XXXX embeds itself in online multiplayer games
  • SCP-XXXX is uneditable or deletable
  • SCP-XXXX generates a fictitious user account: SCP-XXXX-1
  • SCP-XXXX-1 always possesses the same username
  • SCP-XXXX-1 is mostly in-active (or AFK), but will randomly enter short “active” states
  • During “active” states, SCP-XXXX-1 is capable of communication and seems to innately know each players interests. Having conversations about said topics.
  • Players who interact with SCP-XXXX-1 will develop a desire to frequent and talk with it, claiming “he is fun to talk to” and “he understands me”.
  • Players will start prioritising surveying SCP-XXXX-1 for it’s next “active” state over important self needs, such as, consumption of victuals, socialising, sleep, etc.
  • Players will show signs of stress and violence when deprived of contact with SCP-XXXX-1.
  • Players exposed for longer than 100 hours will express dysphoria

Central Narrative: This article will be written according to the standard layout. Starting with containment procedures, a description and finishing with an addendum.

containment procedures will outline only monitoring instructions for the host game ( including a cover-up story for participating publishing companies to grant the SCP foundation moderation privileges in addition to the games code). Players coming into "contact" with SCP-XXXX-1 are automatically added to foundation listings for interviews and eventual administration of amnestics. Because of its shifting nature, it is considered "not contained". However, due to SCP-XXXX-1 always manifesting with the same username (making identifying affected games an easier task), it has been classed as Euclid.

The description will detail SCP-XXXX’s nature and it's odd properties. In addition to, SCP-XXXX-1's description, behavioural patterns and anomalous properties and effects on players and how to recover from the latter.

The addendum will feature the discovery of SCP-XXXX told via the downfall of a Foundation monitoring team tasks with SCP-XXXX-1’s surveillance.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This article seeks to create a fictitious origin for extreme IAD (Internet addiction disorder). In addition, this article is inspired by the collective input of the ChilloutVR community, by an inside joke/meme (hence "Joke SCP") of this very SCP joked to be the source of users who spend their lives in virtual reality (and by extension any other online multiplayers)

Additional Notes: I have a few concerns about copyright. Due to the nature of this article, it will rely heavily on existing games and companies to create the narrative. Am I allowed to use the names of existing companies?
